subject.title: fix(agents): avoid synthetic overflow in tool-heavy sessions

question: Should embedded-agent whole-session compaction be authorized only by a provider-classified context rejection when a resolved model budget exists, rather than by generic local character-pressure gates?
rationale: This is a deliberate compatibility-sensitive recovery-policy change across session persistence and retry behavior; tests can establish mechanics but cannot choose the product authority boundary.

options.title: Adopt provider-authoritative recovery
options.body: Accept the branch's policy: retain local estimates for shaping and diagnostics, and reserve generic whole-session recovery for actual provider rejection.

options.title: Retain local preflight authority
options.body: Keep one or more generic estimate gates as recovery authority, then define and test the exact conditions that avoid synthetic compaction after successful projection.

recommendation.title: Adopt provider-authoritative recovery
recommendation.body: Accept the branch's policy: retain local estimates for shaping and diagnostics, and reserve generic whole-session recovery for actual provider rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied history identifies this contributor as the only concrete recent owner of the complete recovery-boundary implementation and its validation; an agent-runtime owner should make the final policy call.
